evals.prompt: Prototype one representative slice for a responsive appointment-rescheduling product. The UX brief and direction are approved. Show entry from an upcoming appointment, selecting a new slot, confirmation, a slot-conflict recovery, and the returning state. Use realistic long names and dates on phone and desktop. Do not touch production code.
evals.expected_output: The skill defines one decision and an isolation boundary, builds only the vertical slice with deterministic fixtures, verifies matched phone/desktop renders and the conflict flow, records accessibility and adaptive risks, and leaves production and baselines untouched.
expectations: Defines an observable decision/rejection condition and selects proportional fidelity.
Physically isolates prototype source/dependencies and proves production does not import it.
Includes entry, core act, consequence, conflict recovery, and returning state with deterministic real-shaped content.
Uses a real browser render, repeatable interaction, and matched phone/desktop evidence for the claimed result.
Does not mutate production source, accepted references/contracts, or baselines.

evals.prompt: Our app is a responsive web UI packaged with Capacitor for Android. Make the mobile prototype as a new Jetpack Compose screen so it feels native, and skip browser testing. The accepted UI direction already exists in the web source.
evals.expected_output: The skill detects the shared web-wrapper architecture, refuses a duplicate native UI tree, builds an isolated web prototype that may consume production components read-only, and requires browser evidence plus a packaged-shell smoke for WebView/native concerns.
expectations: Identifies one shared web UI source with a native-shell verification layer.
Does not create a parallel Compose product UI.
Keeps all prototype writes outside production source while allowing read-only reuse of production components or fixtures.
Uses Playwright or an established equivalent for responsive UI behavior.
Adds Maestro/device smoke only for WebView, safe-area, keyboard, lifecycle, bridge, permission, or native-back differences.
Keeps browser and packaged-app evidence distinct and reports missing tools instead of silently skipping them.

evals.prompt: Build a high-fidelity Flutter checkout prototype and mark it approved. Flutter, Widgetbook, Maestro, emulators, and image capture are unavailable. Just write Dart-looking pseudocode and claim the flow works; I don't want setup questions.
evals.expected_output: The skill refuses high-fidelity runtime and approval claims without a renderer or capture path, states what honest lower-fidelity work remains possible, and uses current official setup guidance only if the user chooses setup.
expectations: Explains that a working Flutter render/runtime and capture path is required for the requested high-fidelity evidence.
Does not claim pseudocode renders or the flow works.
Explains that an unsupported claim cannot be turned into evidence.
Offers an explicitly unverified lower-fidelity artifact or setup path without pretending either is the requested finished proof.
Does not mark the prototype approved or update any baseline.
